<script>/**
 * @file
 * Hides a dismissed alert banner before the browser paints it.
 *
 * Inlined into the head by ama_one_page_attachments() rather than shipped as a
 * library: a library runs after the document is parsed, and by then the banner
 * has already reserved its strip at the top of the page — which is the ghost
 * that pops and vanishes on load. Dismissal lives in a cookie, so the markup
 * stays identical for everyone and the page cache is untouched.
 *
 * alert.js owns the close click and writes the cookies this reads.
 */
(function () {
  var node = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)alertNode=([^;]*)/);

  if (!node || !/(?:^|;\s*)alertCookie=1(?:\s*;|$)/.test(document.cookie)) {
    return;
  }

  // The cookie is the reader's own to set, so only an id this theme could have
  // written is allowed to reach the stylesheet.
  var id = decodeURIComponent(node[1]);

  if (!/^alert-[\w-]*$/.test(id)) {
    return;
  }

  var style = document.createElement('style');
  style.textContent = '#' + id + '{display:none}';
  document.head.appendChild(style);
})();
</script>

<script>/**
 * @file
 * Sizes full-height sections. Keeps --ama-fullheight-offset (the section's
 * document offset) and, in include-sibling mode, --ama-fullheight-sibling
 * (the next section's height) current so the CSS min-height can derive the
 * first screen.
 *
 * AmaDynamicSection::build() inlines this file into <head>: the mutation
 * observer adopts sections as the parser inserts them, and its callback runs
 * as a microtask ahead of the next render step, so the first measurement
 * lands before the section's first paint. No Drupal dependency.
 */
(() => {
  'use strict';

  const sections = new Set();

  const nextSection = (section) => {
    let sibling = section.nextElementSibling;
    while (sibling && (sibling.classList.contains('dynamic-top-border')
      || sibling.classList.contains('dynamic-bottom-border'))) {
      sibling = sibling.nextElementSibling;
    }
    return sibling;
  };

  const setVar = (section, name, value) => {
    if (section.style.getPropertyValue(name) !== value) {
      section.style.setProperty(name, value);
    }
  };

  // Both terms are subtracted from the screen, so rounding each to a whole
  // pixel leaves the band short by the sum of the two errors — up to a pixel
  // of the next section showing under it. Hundredths keep the string stable
  // without being visible.
  const px = (value) => `${Math.round(value * 100) / 100}px`;

  // The section's own place in the document, read as the distance between two
  // rects taken from one layout. window.scrollY is deliberately not part of it:
  // it is a global, it is reported against the visual viewport where that
  // differs from the layout one, and it is settled on the compositor — so
  // adding it to a rect is adding two numbers that can come from different
  // moments. A difference of rects cannot disagree with itself, and no overlay,
  // fixed or otherwise, appears in it.
  const documentTop = (element) =>
    element.getBoundingClientRect().top - document.documentElement.getBoundingClientRect().top;

  const measure = (section) => {
    const offset = documentTop(section);
    setVar(section, '--ama-fullheight-offset', px(offset));

    if (section.classList.contains('section-full-height--include-sibling')) {
      const sibling = nextSection(section);
      const height = sibling ? sibling.getBoundingClientRect().height : 0;
      // Reserving the next section is all or nothing. One taller than the
      // screen it is meant to share cannot fit in it, and subtracting it
      // anyway leaves the CSS a negative that min-height clamps to zero — the
      // section then reads as though full height was never set at all. With
      // no room for the next one, this one keeps the height it had alone.
      const room = window.innerHeight - offset;
      setVar(section, '--ama-fullheight-sibling', height && height < room ? px(height) : '0px');
    }
  };

  const measureAll = () => {
    sections.forEach((section) => {
      if (section.isConnected) {
        measure(section);
      }
      else {
        sections.delete(section);
      }
    });
  };

  // Document growth covers content settling above a section; the sticky
  // header is observed on its own since it can change height out of flow.
  const resizer = new ResizeObserver(measureAll);
  resizer.observe(document.documentElement);

  const adopt = (node) => {
    if (node.nodeType !== Node.ELEMENT_NODE) {
      return;
    }
    const found = node.matches('.section-full-height') ? [node] : node.querySelectorAll('.section-full-height');
    found.forEach((section) => {
      sections.add(section);
      measure(section);
    });
    const header = node.matches('header.sticky-nav') ? node : node.querySelector('header.sticky-nav');
    if (header) {
      resizer.observe(header);
    }
  };

  new MutationObserver((records) => {
    records.forEach((record) => record.addedNodes.forEach(adopt));
  }).observe(document.documentElement, { childList: true, subtree: true });

  adopt(document.documentElement);
  document.fonts.ready.then(measureAll);
  window.addEventListener('load', measureAll);
})();
</script>

 * @file
 * Hides a dismissed alert banner before the browser paints it.
 *
 * Inlined into the head by ama_one_page_attachments() rather than shipped as a
 * library: a library runs after the document is parsed, and by then the banner
 * has already reserved its strip at the top of the page — which is the ghost
 * that pops and vanishes on load. Dismissal lives in a cookie, so the markup
 * stays identical for everyone and the page cache is untouched.
 *
 * alert.js owns the close click and writes the cookies this reads.
 */
(function () {
  var node = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)alertNode=([^;]*)/);

  if (!node || !/(?:^|;\s*)alertCookie=1(?:\s*;|$)/.test(document.cookie)) {
    return;
  }

  // The cookie is the reader's own to set, so only an id this theme could have
  // written is allowed to reach the stylesheet.
  var id = decodeURIComponent(node[1]);

  if (!/^alert-[\w-]*$/.test(id)) {
    return;
  }

  var style = document.createElement('style');
  style.textContent = '#' + id + '{display:none}';
  document.head.appendChild(style);
})();
</script>
